blocks.html: Since March, 10% of traffic in seven flows has received the original pre-Zee emails while 90% receives ours. Same traffic, same products, one variable: our work. Five months in, here is what the trial says.

blocks.title: Holdout: our versions vs the originals

blocks.html:
Every flow with revenue in it is ahead, per person reached. The two groups are different sizes (10% vs 90%), so everything is compared per person first, then scaled: blended, the originals earn $0.81 per person and ours earn $1.13, a +39.9% lift. Scaled to the full audience over the window, that is $39,821 vs $28,460.

FlowOriginal $/personOurs $/personLift
Site Abandon$0.48$1.07+126%
Cart Abandon$2.00$3.80+90%
Checkout Abandon$3.89$5.40+39%
Bounce Back$0.80$1.04+31%
Welcome$1.76$2.16+23%
All seven blended$0.81$1.13+39.9%

The gap is widening. +21.3% on 21 May, +26.5% on 26 May, +39.9% today. Every test winner rolls into the 90% path permanently while the holdout stands still.

Bounce Back completed its turnaround. Losing at three months, we asked for runway; it is +31% over the full window and ran at +161% in the last 90 days.

The scoreboard. March vs August (26 days, projected).

Klaviyo share climbed from 10.84% to 12.25%, and credit where it is due: most of that climb came from your team’s campaigns, up 62.6%. Our flows held pace with a store growing 19%, and the holdout shows what holding pace took: without the rebuild, the flows would be earning 29% less per person. Combined, the email channel is on the Bomber Eyewear path (9.65% to 16.90% share in nine months), with both engines feeding it.

blocks.title: Subscription revenue, 30-day windows

blocks.html: Subscription revenue: +63.5% since March, +39.8% year on year. The fastest-compounding number in the business, and the post-purchase and subscriber flows are part of the infrastructure holding the curve up.

The acquisition wave converted. Returning share dipped to 62% in May while acquisition fired. It is back to 72%, and returning revenue is up 17.5% on March.

 MarchLast 30 daysChange
Returning customer revenue$112,686$132,421+17.5%
New customer revenue$49,107$51,297+4.5%
Returning % of total69.7%72.1%+2.4pp

Straight attribution: most of that returning number is the subscription base compounding on its own. Our part is narrower and provable: the lifecycle flows defend the base at its leak points (billing failed, cancellations, upcoming charge), and Bounce Back converts one-time buyers to a second order, with a controlled +161% holdout read in the last 90 days. We claim the defence and the nudge, not the whole recovery.

blocks.html: More volume, less friction. You are mailing more people, more often, and annoying fewer of them. The list flipped from shrinking to growing, and that is the foundation everything else compounds on.

blocks.title: The testing engine vs flow revenue

blocks.html: 180 days of work, in five numbers. Since 10 March: 105 hotfixes (82 at three months), 83 new messages launched (was 24), 100 tests wrapped, 30 winners now permanent, and 59% of decisive tests went our way. Losing variants never touch the 90% main path, so testing costs nothing and every win is banked.

August figures are 26 days of actuals projected to month end; every other month is complete. The holdout window is 1 April to 27 August: the test was established on 13 March, a configuration fault in the first two weeks (a delay that stopped the holdout group receiving email) was found and fixed on 27 March, and 1 April was agreed at the 3-month review as the clean start, allowing profiles to filter through evenly first. The comparison uses each branch’s first-message delivery count as the traffic denominator, the same method as the 3-month report. The measured holdout share varies by flow (4.5% to 10%) because delivery differs by branch; the per-person comparison is unaffected by group size. The 10% slices are small by design, from 68 to 1,390 people per flow, which is why lift numbers move as samples grow; the fix for small samples is time, an argument for leaving the holdout running, not ending it. Klaviyo attribution is not incrementality; the holdout is the controlled read, which is why it leads this review. All revenue is Klaviyo-attributed Placed Order unless stated otherwise.

Next 90 days: let the holdouts mature (the Bounce Back flip took five months to prove), keep compounding Welcome, the highest-traffic flow in the account, extend the abandonment ladder to the remaining gaps in the map, and keep feeding the subscription engine.

The 3-month review asked for runway. Six months in: share is climbing, the losing flow is now a win, and the gap against the originals widens every month we run.

reports.summary: A five-month holdout proves our flow versions out-earn the originals by 40% at equivalent traffic. Share of revenue is climbing, the list flipped to growth, and the gap widens every month.
